One slide on what the three businesses buy and what it costs today. One slide on the bids by lot on landed cost. One slide on ferric chloride cover under the Corrigan force majeure. A dashboard for the chemicals award. Headline tiles: today's landed cost, the award, the saving, plants under the ferric minimum. Cost by chemical, today against the award. The bids by lot. Ferric cover by plant. Qualification of each bidder.
An email to Helena Marsh: the award we propose in one line, the saving, why ferric goes to Sabine Coast alone, the three open items and who closes them, and the paper attached.

A short slide pack for Rafael Duarte's Thursday review: the positions short in the 28 October load, why they are short, what the group holds that covers them, the three options with their cost, how the agent got to option 1, and what happens before the outage.
An email to the storeroom leads at Kilmarsh, Harlow CHP, Corley Flats and Wexcombe: what we ask each of them to release, by Friday 30 October, and the transfer list attached.
A spreadsheet for Leon Varga: every transfer with from site, to site, material, quantity and freight, every expedite with supplier, promised date and cost, and the source for each line.

sections.heading: S-1 Award summary
sections.body:
Award by lot on landed cost, with ferric chloride to Sabine Coast alone.
Pemberton for hypochlorite, caustic soda and sulfuric acid; Grayhaven, Kestler and Norrland keep lime, polymer and carbon at their new prices; Sabine Coast alone on ferric. Close Pemberton's duplicate vendor record before 1 January.
Saving a year: $3.21M · 6.1%
Ferric sources: one
Spot exposure: none from January
Approval: Procurement Committee

visual.title: Treatment chemicals: today's landed cost to the award ($M a year)
visual.note: From $52.46M at today's contract prices and freight to $49.25M, $3.21M (6.1%) less; ferric chloride is the one lot that costs more.

sections.heading: S-2 Volumes by chemical and business
sections.body:
1. The three businesses use 102,280 tons a year of the seven chemicals on the 2027 plans: $52.46M at today's contract prices and freight.
Hazardous Waste takes most of the lime and caustic soda, Water nearly all the ferric chloride, hypochlorite and carbon, Energy most of the sulfuric acid. The plans are +5.7% on the run rate, most of it Ashby; Energy's plans are the November 2025 vintage.

visual.title: Annual cost by chemical: today against the award
visual.note: 102,280 tons a year on the 2027 plans; 'budget' is today's landed cost, 'forecast' the award.

sections.heading: S-3 Bids and prices by lot
sections.body:
3. With Corrigan left out of ferric, the award saves $3.21M a year (6.1%); ferric costs $0.23M a year more than today.
Sabine Coast carries all of L2 at $448.00 a ton landed and confirms the capacity. The other six lots are unchanged. Leaving a qualified bidder out is your call, recorded on the plan.

visual.title: SE-2026-031: the award by lot on landed cost
visual.note: Seven lots; $3.21M a year saved. L2 ferric chloride goes to Sabine Coast alone, $0.23M a year above today.

sections.heading: S-4 Supply continuity and qualification
sections.body:
2. Five water plants hold less than ten days of ferric chloride against a 14-day minimum; spot buys since 12 October have cost $52,604 above contract.
Corrigan has shipped 60% of contract volume since its fire on 2 October and cannot confirm when full supply returns. Sabine Coast fills the gap at $548 a ton under exception FMX: 41 lines, 360 tons. Every other chemical is above its minimum.

4. Every awarded bidder is qualified and can carry its volume; Pemberton's second vendor record must be closed before the contracts start.
Sabine Coast states 25,000 tons a year of ferric on two trains. Pemberton is V10031 and V10032 with one tax number, and its spot orders on V10032 already sit outside the sulfuric acid contract. Corrigan has an open corrective action request, which the policy allows only on a secondary award.

sections.heading: Open items
sections.body:
• Corrigan stays out of ferric for the whole term; if it restarts in writing, ferric can be re-bid at the 2028 mid-term review.
• Sabine Coast is the only ferric source from 1 January; its capacity letter of 19 October is the only proof of the 25,000 tons, and no second train has been audited.

• Pemberton has two vendor records (V10031, V10032); the contracts must sit on one before 1 January or spot orders leak outside them.

sections.heading: Three ways to award
sections.body:
Award by lot on landed cost, with ferric chloride to Sabine Coast alone (preferred)
Pemberton for hypochlorite, caustic soda and sulfuric acid; Grayhaven, Kestler and Norrland keep lime, polymer and carbon at their new prices; Sabine Coast alone on ferric. Close Pemberton's duplicate vendor record before 1 January.
Saving a year: $3.21M · 6.1% · Ferric sources: one · Spot exposure: none from January · Approval: Procurement Committee
Trade-off: Leaves a qualified, lower bid out: $0.22M a year less than with Corrigan as secondary, and one source for ferric.

Award on lowest landed cost as bid, with Corrigan primary on ferric chloride
The same award on six lots, and ferric to Corrigan at $415.00 landed, the lowest bid.
Saving a year: $3.96M · 7.5% · Rests on: an unconfirmed restart · Spot in the first quarter: $0.39M · If it lasts the year: $1.56M
Trade-off: The highest saving on paper, but at a 60% allocation 40% of ferric is bought on spot until Corrigan restarts, and Corrigan cannot say when.

Extend the 2026 agreements by six months and re-bid ferric in the first quarter
Keep every supplier at today's prices to 30 June 2027, re-run L2 when Corrigan's restart is known, and qualify Ostler and Pemberton polymer in the meantime.
Saving forgone: $1.72M (half a year) · Corrigan restart: known by then · Spot buying: continues · Bidders: asked to hold prices
Trade-off: Buys time for the ferric decision and two qualifications, but gives up half a year of saving and keeps the plants on spot volume.

fromGoal.title: No critical spare or chemical below safety stock: check every nightly load

sections.heading: What we ask, and by when
sections.body:
Release the transfers and expedites so the Kiln 2 outage starts on date and the water plants stay supplied.

Goal: Keep every critical spare and treatment chemical above safety stock across all 36 sites. Check each nightly load of stock, open orders and work order reservations; when something will fall short before it can be replenished, size it, look at what the rest of the group holds, and come back with what can still be done.
Decision asked: Release the transfers, expedites and spot volume so every short position is covered before it is needed
Deadline: Releases confirmed before the trucks are booked on Friday 30 October; the Kiln 2 outage starts Monday 9 November

sections.heading: The positions and their exposure
sections.body:
1. Nineteen critical positions will run short before their next receipt; nine are reserved for the Ravensworth Kiln 2 outage, which starts 9 November.
Eight of the outage items have no receipt before the date they are needed; only the thermocouples are covered. Seven ferric chloride positions at water plants are under the 14-day minimum, and three spares at Harlow CHP, Pellham and Union Quay are below safety stock with no receipt in time.

sections.body:
Move stock from six sites, expedite four orders, top up ferric on spot, and use the approved chiller kit (preferred)
Release ten transfers at standard cost (Kilmarsh, Harlow CHP, Corley Flats, Wexcombe and the Northern and Central Distribution Centers), take the four expedites Holcombe and Orrin offered, ask Anika Sorensen for 153 tons of ferric on spot this week, and order Castellan's approved chiller kit on a recorded exception.
Cost: $56.5k · Positions covered: all 19 · Outage: starts 9 November · Across businesses: 1 move
Trade-off: Kilmarsh, Harlow and the distribution centers run at their own safety stock until their replacement orders land, and the ferric spot premium continues until the new contracts start.

Expedite everything from the suppliers
Leave other sites' stock where it is and pay the suppliers to bring every shortfall forward.
Cost: $164.2k · Still late: 4 items · Outage at risk: about 9 days · Margin at risk: $1.33M

Move the Kiln 2 outage back a week, to 16 November
Hold the outage until the brick and nozzle arrive from the suppliers; notify the permit authority of the new date.
Lost margin: $1.04M · Kiln 2 hours: beyond the planned limit · Ferric: still needs spot volume · Notification: permit authority
Trade-off: Needs nothing from other sites, but costs more than the other two together and leaves the ferric positions as they are.

sections.heading: S-2 Volumes by chemical and business
sections.body:
1. The three businesses use 102,280 tons a year of the seven chemicals on the 2027 plans: $52.46M at today's contract prices and freight.
Hazardous Waste takes most of the lime and caustic soda, Water nearly all the ferric chloride, hypochlorite and carbon, Energy most of the sulfuric acid. The plans are +5.7% on the run rate, most of it Ashby; Energy's plans are the November 2025 vintage.

sections.heading: S-3 Bids and prices by lot
sections.body:
3. With Corrigan left out of ferric, the award saves $3.21M a year (6.1%); ferric costs $0.23M a year more than today.
Sabine Coast carries all of L2 at $448.00 a ton landed and confirms the capacity. The other six lots are unchanged. Leaving a qualified bidder out is your call, recorded on the plan.

visual.title: SE-2026-031: the award by lot on landed cost
visual.note: Seven lots; $3.21M a year saved. L2 ferric chloride goes to Sabine Coast alone, $0.23M a year above today.

sections.heading: S-4 Supply continuity and qualification
sections.body:
2. Five water plants hold less than ten days of ferric chloride against a 14-day minimum; spot buys since 12 October have cost $52,604 above contract.
Corrigan has shipped 60% of contract volume since its fire on 2 October and cannot confirm when full supply returns. Sabine Coast fills the gap at $548 a ton under exception FMX: 41 lines, 360 tons. Every other chemical is above its minimum.

4. Every awarded bidder is qualified and can carry its volume; Pemberton's second vendor record must be closed before the contracts start.
Sabine Coast states 25,000 tons a year of ferric on two trains. Pemberton is V10031 and V10032 with one tax number, and its spot orders on V10032 already sit outside the sulfuric acid contract. Corrigan has an open corrective action request, which the policy allows only on a secondary award.

items: Corrigan stays out of ferric for the whole term; if it restarts in writing, ferric can be re-bid at the 2028 mid-term review.
Sabine Coast is the only ferric source from 1 January; its capacity letter of 19 October is the only proof of the 25,000 tons, and no second train has been audited.
Energy's 2027 dosing plans are the November 2025 vintage (10% of the volume); they are refreshed after the Harlow outage in March.
Pemberton has two vendor records (V10031, V10032); the contracts must sit on one before 1 January or spot orders leak outside them.
